timing: Exploratory addition after the initial pair-count, qualifying-center-count and maximum-local-Z results were examined; frozen before computing component-extent null results. Initial protocol and outputs remain unchanged.
reason: The user asked whether mapped neighborhoods are unusually spatially enriched. A maximum single-center statistic need not detect an extended connected neighborhood. Test the size of the actual originally defined connected neighborhoods directly.
definition: Use original 100 micrometer radius and >=20 tumor cells, >=5 coexpressing cells, >=10% coexpression thresholds without change. Connect qualifying centers within 100 micrometers and take the maximum number of centers in any component. Recompute the full component search for each shuffled realization.
configurations: Primary coexpression marks, 100 micrometers, all three sections and all three original nulls; same 1999 random realizations and seeds as the initial run, verified by reproducing pair-count and qualifying-center statistics.
component_p: Compare each original component's center count to the null distribution of the maximum component size over the whole section. Report (1+b)/(1+1999), three-section Bonferroni and six-comparison Bonferroni accounting for the two localization statistics (local peak and component extent) across three sections, within each explicit null.
global_multiplicity: Holm over nine maximum-extent configurations; additionally Holm over all 30 earlier maximum-local-Z configurations plus nine maximum-extent configurations, to expose sensitivity to the added localization statistic.
limits: Region-level significance applies to the connected set under the fixed search rule and null; no inference that every member cell is a distinct biological state. Different nulls answer different conditional questions. Report all earlier negative localization and nuclear findings. This is not a pre-analysis primary test.
